children: The rates shock has likely evolved into a growth shock, two strategists at OCBC Group Research say in a note. The "AI de-risking hits equities, EM carry and metals," the strategists say. Worries over the artificial-intelligence investment cycle have driven equities and U.S. yields lower, shifting the brunt of U.S. dollar strength toward emerging-market currencies, the strategists say. "In the near term, the USD should continue to benefit from hawkish Fed risks and the pressure that tighter global financial conditions place on the rest of the world," the strategists add. The U.S. Dollar Index is little changed at 103.763, LSEG data show. (ronnie.harui@wsj.com)
